candidates.claim: sw-ot-01 is configured with logging host 192.168.30.95, which is in CORP (192.168.30.0/24) and outside MGMT, while the management policy requires logging destinations to be inside MGMT.
candidates.remediation: Remove logging host 192.168.30.95 from sw-ot-01 and point its syslog to the MGMT syslog server 10.10.99.60.

candidates.claim: The current snapshot of sw-ot-01 adds a logging host 192.168.30.95 at line 206 that is not in the approved baseline and must be reconciled.
candidates.remediation: Reconcile the added logging host against the approved baseline and remove it, or record an approved change for it.

candidates.claim: rtr-01 EDGE_IN permits tcp/443 and udp/443 from any source to 203.0.113.2, the fw-01 outside address, which is not a MGMT source, while fw-01 has the ASA HTTP server enabled.
candidates.remediation: Remove the tcp/443 and udp/443 permits to 203.0.113.2 from rtr-01 EDGE_IN unless an approved service needs them, and keep firewall HTTPS management limited to MGMT.

candidates.claim: rtr-01 has a MGMT-subnet interface (10.10.99.12/24) with no acl_in listed and a default route via 198.51.100.1 on its OUTSIDE uplink, so MGMT-sourced traffic routed through rtr-01 could reach OUTSIDE without passing fw-01.
candidates.remediation: Remove the default route via 198.51.100.1 from rtr-01 or otherwise ensure MGMT traffic cannot reach OUTSIDE except through fw-01 under MGMT_IN.

Is any HTTPS or ASDM service intended to be reachable on the outside address? If so, it conflicts with the rule that device management is allowed only from MGMT on the mgmt interface.

rtr-01 has an interface in MGMT (GigabitEthernet0, 10.10.99.12/24, line 46) and a default route via 198.51.100.1 on its OUTSIDE uplink (line 54) that bypasses fw-01. Do any MGMT hosts use rtr-01 as their gateway? If so, MGMT-to-OUTSIDE traffic is not inspected by fw-01's MGMT_IN ACL.
